newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols jump as stocks slide.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols jump as stocks slide.

text.p: A big slide in stock prices, compounded by expiration of July options, propelled implied volatilities for U.S. stock index options sharply higher, traders said.

"They hit the tech stocks pretty hard, and with bonds also going down they hit the broader market," said Jesse Stamer of TradeNet, a designated primary market maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange. "Vols are spiking up all over the floor."
The S&P 100 index fell more than 15 points to a low of 892.33 in early trade before clawing back slightly.

The selloff was triggered by a downturn in Microsoft Corp shares after the firm's quarterly earnings results late Thursday. Although earnings were sharply higher from a year earlier they failed to please the Street, and Microsoft also predicted weakness in the current quarter.
Traders said the downturn in Microsoft stock, one of the leaders of the market's recent tech-centered rally, poured cold water on the market.
Out-of-the-money put sellers, who had been benefiting from the market's long bull run, were jolted by a sudden surge of negative gamma in their July positions, they said.
July 900 OEX puts had the largest volume among puts, trading 12,300 contracts by 1115 CDT/1615 GMT against open interest at Thursday's close of 11,185 contracts.
The 900 puts were 10 points out-of-the-money at Thursday's close, but instead of expiring worthless today they saw their premium shoot up as high as 10 from Thursday's close of 1.
July 910 puts, which at Thursday's close were priced at 2-15/16, rose to a high of 18 and traded more than 8,000 lots.
Short-dated at-the-money options have high gamma, which provides quick premium acceleration, although they are vulnerable to time decay in a quiet market.
The CBOE volatility index was up 2.30 point at 26.44 at 1115 CDT/1615 GMT after spiking up toward 28 earlier in the initial panic.

The abrupt downturn, particularly coming at an option expiration, could have a long-lasting effect on the market's behavior, traders said. July options end trading today and expire, technically, on Saturday.
"I think there will be some followthrough on Monday," said Jerry Hegarty, an equity analyst at Thomson Research. "People will get nervous over the weekend, and Monday could really be ugly."
The buy-on-dips attitude that has persisted in recent months now looked less likely to be rewarded, Hegarty said.
He said the market's performance this afternoon could be critical.
"This is the first time that we've been weak this much this early in the day in quite a while," he said. "This is really now a test of fortitude."
Stamer at TradeNet said the market would probably remain jittery into early August, when most earnings results will have come out.
